title: Excess Obstructions and Layer-Contained Certificates for the Hypergraph Nash--Williams--Tutte Conjecture
summary: Guo, Li, Shangguan, Tamo, and Wootters proposed a hypergraph analogue of the Nash--Williams--Tutte theorem, asserting that every $k$-weakly-partition-connected hypergraph admits a $k$-distinguishable tree assignment. We identify a sharp edge-count obstruction to the literal statement. A full tree assignment has $ρ(H)=\sum_{e\in E(H)}(|e|-1)$ labelled graph edges, whereas an ordered decomposition into $k$ spanning trees has exactly $k(t-1)$ edges.
